findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate `adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py` (`_translate_create_fields` / `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound`, `:40`/`:111`) as a second gated DC CREATE consumer that must render (`render_markdown_to_wiki`/`to_wire`) before `fit_outbound`, or state why that path is out of scope.
evidence: _issues.py:40 `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()`
_issues.py:111 `fields["description"] = _DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)`
_issues.py:174 `fields = _translate_create_fields(ticket_data)` inside `create_issue`
Plan names only `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:57) as the CREATE path that 'must also render before the fit'
Existing test `test_dc_create_path_fits_description_through_the_wiki_codec` confirms this create path is live/characterized
findings.finding: The plan identifies backend.py:_map_local_to_dc_fields as the DC CREATE path that fits description without rendering (needs to_wire before fit), but a SECOND DC create-side path with the identical defect is not enumerated: adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py builds `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()` (:40) and applies only `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)` (:111) inside `_translate_create_fields` (:93), which is invoked by `create_issue` (:174). Post-cutover this path ships RAW Markdown on DC create, defeating the 'issue.update/CREATE gets rendered wiki' guarantee for issues created through the REST client.
findings.location: The live cutover → DC (CREATE) section; Scope (IN)
scenarios: A brand-new local ticket is created on a DC instance through the REST client path (_issues.create_issue) after the cutover flag is enabled: its Markdown description is fitted but never rendered to wiki, so it lands as raw Markdown
findings.suggested_fix: Add `_issues.py` to Scope (IN) alongside backend.py's CREATE path and require the same render-before-fit change (gated), plus a create-through-_issues convergence assertion.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the non-idempotent round-trip tail (the ~0.35% marklas measured) is handled — e.g. a bounded/one-shot re-emit guard or a per-binding churn detector — and add an AC/test that a non-idempotent body does not re-emit unboundedly across passes.
evidence: Plan: 'once-only re-emit convergence holds iff the codec law ... holds ... plus marklas's 99.65% round-trip idempotence — hence no post-push GET'
99.65% idempotence implies a ~0.35% tail where normalize_outbound(local) != decode_inbound(wire_jira_stored)

Live: diff_canonical_fields (outbound_field_diff.py:352) and _local_matches_baseline (:476) compare against canonical_baseline = decode_inbound(baseline_wire); a non-idempotent body makes local != baseline permanently
No AC bounds the re-emit count for a non-idempotent body; test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes asserts convergence but does not exercise the non-idempotent minority
findings.finding: Once-only convergence is staked entirely on the codec law plus marklas's 99.65% round-trip idempotence with 'no post-push GET', but the ~0.35% non-idempotent tail is unhandled: for a body where decode(to_wire(local)) != decode(wire Jira echoes back), the normalized local never matches decode(baseline_wire), so local!=baseline holds every pass and the description re-emits forever with no bounded-re-emit or churn-detection guard.
findings.location: Context/Problem ('hence no post-push GET') and Design decisions #1; Acceptance Criteria (test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes / test_recanonicalization_converges)
scenarios: A DC wiki body that renders and re-renders non-idempotently (in the 0.35% tail) is edited once; every subsequent no-edit pass re-emits the same description update
A Cloud ADF body outside the round-trip fixed point loops similarly
findings.suggested_fix: Add a change-gated re-emit guard keyed on the stored rich_sha: once a description has been pushed and its wire echo has been baselined, suppress a further identical push unless local (not its normalization) actually changed, so a non-idempotent body re-emits at most once instead of every pass; cover it with a test using a deliberately non-idempotent codec stub.

findings.finding: The rollback/cutover flag — a new config/flag that AC8 requires to default OFF and that both the Cloud and DC cutover Scope lines call 'gated' — has no named edit target in the Scope edit-set. It is a CREATION (new behavioral surface) that gates the codec-selection/send path, yet no config module or symbol is enumerated to define/read it.
findings.location: Scope section (Cloud/DC '(gated)' lines) + Rollback paragraph + AC8 (test_cutover_defaults_off / test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Scope bullet naming where the flag is defined (e.g., a REBAR_RECONCILER_RICH_TEXT_CUTOVER_<CLIENT> constant in src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py) and the exact read site(s) that select the Markdown-aware vs plain/identity path per client, so AC8's tests have a named target.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete read-path/done-definition that consumes the inline rich_sha (which compare or convergence step reads it), or drop it and rely on the origin-gating (local != baseline) the ACs already exercise.
evidence: Design decision 4 states echo suppression is driven by origin-gating: 'An update fires only when local != baseline' — the rich_sha compare is separately noted to 'never write back'.

Every suppression/convergence AC (test_echo_rebar_origin_only, test_recanonicalization_converges, test_jira_native_construct_survives, test_lossy_body_converges_across_passes) is framed on local!=baseline / normalize_outbound compares, none on rich_sha.
The rich_sha's sole AC is a storage-profile check ('<=0.07 KB/version'), i.e. it verifies the artifact is cheap to store, not that any code path consumes it.
peer_state.py:38 _BASELINE_FIELDS is the existing per-binding stored state; rich_sha is an addition to that schema with no named reader.
findings.finding: The inline change-gated rich_sha is a new stored artifact whose only acceptance criterion is a storage-cost profile; no suppression/convergence AC reads it, so its current-done-definition purpose is unstated (YAGNI risk).
findings.location: Design decisions #4 ('Store a change-gated rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16] inline in the binding') and the AC 'The rich layer stores an inline change-gated 8-byte rich_sha ... verified by the git-delta harness at <=0.07 KB/version'
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks what reads rich_sha and finds only a size test.
The field is persisted every version but never queried, becoming dead schema.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State which code path writes the inline `rich_sha` and when (e.g. within `_advance_baselines` alongside the baseline), so its create/update lifecycle is unambiguous.
evidence: 'Store a change-gated `rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` (8 bytes) inline in the binding ... the compare never writes back.'
'`_advance_baselines` (`reconcile_helpers.py:602`) as sole baseline writer'
findings.finding: The plan introduces an inline `rich_sha` binding field but does not state which component writes it or when, given `_advance_baselines` is named the 'sole baseline writer' yet Decision 4 says 'the compare never writes back.'
scenarios: An executor must decide whether rich_sha is written by _advance_baselines alongside the baseline or by a separate path, affecting the CREATE/UPDATE lifecycle.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that `_advance_baselines` writes `rich_sha` atomically with the baseline on push-success, and that the compare path only reads it.

findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` shared state names a CREATE site (inline beside `_BASELINE_FIELDS`) and a change-gated semantics, and asserts 'The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back' — but it does not name the WRITER that advances `rich_sha` when the rendered wire actually changes. The plan reuses `_advance_baselines` for the baseline but does not state whether that same single writer also updates `rich_sha`, leaving update-ownership/concurrency for the new field unspecified.
findings.location: Origin-gating section ('store a change-gated rich_sha … inline in the binding') and Scope: binding_store.py
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly that `rich_sha` is advanced by the same `_advance_baselines` persist writer from `ctx.curr_snapshot`, gated on `sha256(rendered_wire)` differing from the stored value, and that no other path mutates it.

findings.finding: The new inline `rich_sha` state names its shape (8-byte sha256 of rendered wire), its change-gate discipline (no per-pass write), and that the compare is read-only, but it never names the WRITER: which function advances `rich_sha` and at what point in the pass. The plan is explicit that `_advance_baselines` is the single existing writer for the baseline and that the compare 'never writes back', which leaves the rich_sha write path unowned — is it a second writer, or is it folded into `_advance_baselines`?
findings.suggested_fix: State that `rich_sha` is advanced by the same single `_advance_baselines` writer at persist (change-gated on rendered-wire delta), so no second writer is introduced.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` codec-law redefinition and its comment-dedup coupling in an ADR / code doc note.
evidence: 'redefine `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`, restoring the codec law'
'The `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` redefinition also reaches the DC comment-diff dedup key'
findings.finding: The plan redefines `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` (a codec contract change with a documented shared-op side effect on the DC comment-diff dedup key) but names no ADR/design-doc update capturing this new contract; it only cites the pre-existing ADR 0026 for baselines.
scenarios: A future maintainer reads WikiTextCodec expecting identity normalize_outbound and is surprised by the decode∘to_wire semantics and its comment-dedup coupling.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short ADR/docstring note recording that WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound == decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) and that comment-diff dedup deliberately uses _IdentityCodec, not WikiTextCodec.
